questions.stemHtml: A patient presented to medicine opd with anxiety and palpitation. Ecg is given below which among the following is not used in the treatment of the condition given below?
questions.solutionHtml:
Adenosine
  • Multifocal atrial tachycardia (MAT) is a cardiac arrhythmia caused by multiple sites of competing atrial activity. It is characterised by an irregular atrial rate greater than 100 beats per minute (bpm).
  • Atrial activity is well organised, with at least 3 morphologically distinct P waves, irregular P-P intervals, and an isoelectric baseline between the P waves
  • Recent guidelines recommend the use of beta-blockers and CCB for rate control and ongoing management of MAT.
  • Adenosine is not used for MAT


Harrison’s principles of internal medicine, 20th edition, Page : 732

questions.stem: Hb is 5gm/dl and absolute reticulocyte count percentage is 9%. Calculate corrected reticulocyte count:
questions.solutionHtml:
3
  • Corrected Reticulocyte count = Reticulocyte % * Actual Hb / Normal Hb
  • So, CRC = 9 * 5/15 = 3


Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page No. 435

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pathology - INI CET NOV 2022 (PART A)
questions.stem: An Elderly patient on a vegetarian diet presented with palor and easy fatiguability. Blood smear showed findings of macrocytic anemia. Other lab findings are given below. Elevated homocysteine and normal methylmalonic acid levels. Megaloblastic anemia present. HB - 9 gm/dl , MCV - 112 fl. Identify diagnosis:
questions.solutionHtml:
Folate deficiency
  • The given clinical scenario of macrocytic anemia in a vegetarian with elevated homocysteine levels is due to megaloblastic anemia, which can be caused by the deficiency of vitamin B12 or folic acid.
  • Vitamin B12 deficiency is associated with raised serum methylmalonic acid (MMA) levels, which are normal in this patient; hence, folic acid deficiency is the cause of megaloblastic anemia in this patient.

Folic acid deficiency is associated with the following clinical and laboratory findings:

  • Raised MCV (normal range: 80-100 fL) - macrocytosis
  • Normal MCHC (normal range: 33-36 g/dL)
  • Increased MCH
  • Decreased reticulocyte count
  • Elevated homocysteine level
  • Normal MMA level


Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page No. 769

questions.stemHtml: The following is a histopathological image of thyroi?. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Medullary Carcinoma Thyroid
  • The given histopathological image shows Polygonal cells with abundant cytoplasm and amyloid deposition which suggests the diagnosis of Medullary carcinoma thyroid.
  • It is a type of thyroid cancer that arises from the parafollicular or C-cells of the thyroid gland. It is associated with the production of calcitonin, which can lead to the deposition of amyloid within the tumor stroma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease 10th Edition, Page No. 1103

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pathology - INI CET NOV 2022 (PART A)
questions.stem: Metastatic calcification can be seen in all these conditions except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Vit D Deficiency
  • Pathologic calcification is the abnormal tissue deposition of calcium salts, together with smaller amounts of iron, magnesium, and other mineral salts. It is of two types namely metastatic and dystrophic calcification.
  • Metastatic calcification is the deposition of calcium salts in otherwise normal tissues. Metastatic calcification refers to a type of soft tissue calcification caused by elevated serum calcium salts
  • Typical locations for metastatic calcification include the lungs and kidneys but the condition can also occur in the liver and heart.

 Aetiology 

  • Chemotherapy
  • Chronic renal failure
  • Milk-alkali syndrome
  • Multiple myeloma
  • Osteolysis from malignant metastasis
  • Primary and secondary hyperparathyroidism
  • Sarcoidosis
  • Vitamin D intoxication


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease 10th Edition, Page No. 25

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pathology - INI CET NOV 2022 (PART A)
questions.stemHtml: Maximum amplitude in thromboelastography image is by?
questions.solutionHtml:
Platelet

Thromboelastography (TEG) is a hemostatic assay that measures the  viscoelastic properties of whole blood clot formation under low shear stress. TEG shows the interaction of platelets with the coagulation cascade

Specific parameters represent the 3 phases of the cell-based model of haemostasis: initiation, amplification, and propagation

  • R value = reaction time (s)- time of latency from start of test to initial fibrin formation (amplitude of 2mm)-initiation phase- dependent on clotting factors
  • K = kinetics (s)- time taken to achieve a certain level of clot strength (amplitude of 20mm)- amplification phase- dependent on fibrinogen
  • alpha = angle (slope of line between R and K)- measures the speed at which fibrin build up and cross-linking takes place, hence assesses the rate of clot formation- propagation phase-dependent on fibrinogen

TMA = time to maximum amplitude(s) 

  • MA = maximum amplitude (mm)-represents the ultimate strength of the fibrin clot; i.e. overall stability of the clot- dependent on platelets (80%) and fibrin (20%)
  • A30 or LY30 = amplitude at 30 minutes-percentage decrease in amplitude at 30 minutes post-MA- fibrinolysis phase


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease 10th Edition, Page No. 902

questions.stemHtml: Identify the instrument shown below:
questions.solutionHtml:
Klima Needle

Klima needle- guard with screw along the length of the needle 

  • Most commonly used for obtaining bone marrow aspirates from the sternum 

Option B  : Salah needle- guard with screw along the side 

  • Most commonly used for obtaining bone marrow aspirates from the sternum are the Salah and Klima needle 

Islam Needle

  • A new bone marrow biopsy needle with core securing device.

Jamshidi needle

It is a cylindrical needle with a tapered cutting tip. The tapered end reduces the potential of crush artifacts. It is the most commonly used needle for performing bone marrow biopsies

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pathology - INI CET NOV 2022 (PART A)
questions.solutionHtml:
E6,E7

HPV is a double-stranded DNA, non enveloped virus primarily spread through sexual contact 

HPV types 16 and 18 are high-risk subtypes for developing a malignancy

  • E6 Genes of HPV : Inactivate p53
  • E7 Gene : Inactivate RB gene 

L1 (Capsid protein) is associated with vaccine production

  • HPV 16 is the most carcinogenic and accounts for 55 to 60% of cervical cancers worldwide.
  • HPV 18 is the second most carcinogenic and accounts for 10 to 15% of cervical cancer. Most malignant is also HPV 18
  • Risk factors such as smoking, immunocompromised state, or HIV infection likely lead to persistence of HPV infection and an increased risk for the development of CIN
  • Colposcopy with directed biopsy is the preferred method for evaluation of an abnormal pap smear result. "Co-testing" combines cytology and HPV testing for high-risk types


Jawetz, Melnick and Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 27th Edition, Page No. 631

questions.stemHtml: A 19 years old girl presents with a 6 month old swelling that moves with deglutition and shows strap muscle invasion. What is the diagnosis:
questions.solutionHtml:
PTC
  • The given clinical scenario and histopathological image showing papillary structures and the presence of Orphan Annie nuclei (nuclei with clear chromatin and grooves) suggests the diagnosis of Papillary Thyroid carcinoma (PTC).
  • It is the most common type of thyroid cancer, especially in young patients. It often presents as a thyroid nodule or swelling and may show movement with swallowing.


Sabiston Textbook of Surgery, 20th Edition, Page No. 925

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pathology - INI CET NOV 2022 (PART A)
questions.stem: A patient with bare lymphocytic disease, graft vs host reaction does not occur due to:

options.label: B
options.text: MHC class I Deficiency on Lymphocytes

options.label: D
options.text: MHC class II Deficiency on Lymphocytes

questions.answerText: MHC class II Deficiency on Lymphocytes
questions.solutionHtml:
MHC class II Deficiency on Lymphocytes

Bare lymphocyte syndrome, a severe combined immunodeficiency due to loss of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II gene expression, is caused by inherited mutations in the genes encoding the heterotrimeric transcription factor RFX (RFX-B, RFX5, and RFXAP) and the class II transactivator CIITA 

  • MHC class II genes encode heterodimeric glycoproteins that present antigens to CD4+ T cells to initiate the acquired arm of the immune response.
  • They are also crucial for determining the repertoire of CD4+ T cells during positive and negative selection in the thymus.
  • Patients with BLS typically present in the first year of life with recurrent infections and have reduced levels of CD4+ T cells.
  • Their humoral immune response is severely impaired as well, and most patients die before reaching puberty


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 244

questions.stem: Egg-shell calcification is seen in all of the following except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Metastatic Lymph Node
  • Egg-shell calcification refers to the deposition of calcified material around the periphery of a structure, giving it the appearance of an eggshell.
  • It is not typically seen in metastatic lymph nodes.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pathology - INI CET NOV 2022 (PART A)
questions.stem: Which of the following statement about sirtuin is not correct:

options.label: C
options.text: Increase Insulin Sensitivity and Support Glucose Metabolism

options.label: D
options.text: It has Histone Deacetylase Activity and cause Chromatin Condensation

questions.solutionHtml:
Stimulated by Nicotinamide
  • Sirtuins are a class of proteins that possess either mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase or deacetylase activity. They have been shown to slow down the aging process.

Sirtuins promote the expression of several genes whose products increase longevity. These include proteins that:

  • Reduce apoptosis
  • Stimulate protein folding
  • Inhibit the harmful effects of oxygen-free radicals
  • Increase insulin sensitivity and glucose metabolism (maybe targeted for the treatment of diabetes)
  • Ensure that damaged DNA is not propagated, preventing the accumulation of mutations
  • Promotes replicative senescence under chronic stress
  • Sirtuins level increases by caloric restriction and are present in red wine.
  • Nicotinamide inhibits sirtuins through the so-called base exchange pathway


Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 68

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pathology - INI CET NOV 2022 (PART A)
questions.stem: Which interleukin not involved in TH 1:
questions.solutionHtml:
IL 4
  • Dendritic cells and macrophages present antigens to T helper cells (TH) after which they differentiate into TH1 and TH2 cells. They are responsible for cell-mediated and humoral immune responses, respectively.
  • IL-12 is secreted by macrophages and promotes the proliferation of TH1 cells.

TH1 cells secrete:

  • IL-2 which activates natural killer cells (NK cells) and cytotoxic T cells
  • Interferon gamma which stimulates macrophages and is also responsible for delayed hypersensitivity along with TGF beta.



Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 99
